newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Saab Auto Jan-Aug sales fall 4 pct.
newsitem.headline: Saab Auto Jan-Aug sales fall 4 pct.

text.p: Swedish vehicle maker Saab Automobile AB sold 66,529 cars between January and August this year which was a four percent drop on the same time a year ago, a company spokesman said on Monday.
Saab Automobile spokesman Olle Wallen told Reuters that sales in the U.S. totalled 19,579 for the first eight months of the year, which was a rise of nine percent compared to the same period in 1995.
Sales in Britain rose to 11,057 from 8,717 in the first eight months of the year. Total sales in Britain in 1995 were 11,534, Wallen said.

But sales in Sweden in the first eight months of 1996 fell to 9,207 from 12,310, due to a worries about a change in taxation on company cars which account for 60 to 70 percent of Saab's sales in Sweden, Wallen said.
However he said the change in legislation would not be as bad as anticipated.
"We understand the market on company cars will come back for the rest of the year," Wallen said.
Saab is jointly owned by Swedish investment group Investor and U.S. vehicle maker General Motors.
